title: pkix-ct: is Apple's CT log list signed, and how?
description:
## What

pkix-ct documents Apple and browser-specific log lists as alternative sources, ingested by constructing CtLog values and calling CtLogList::insert. PKIX-eits added signature verification for Google's list; Apple's was out of scope there and was not investigated.

## Questions

1. Does Apple publish a detached signature over its log list, and with what key and algorithm? Google publishes log_list.json, log_list.sig and log_list_pubkey.pem; Apple's distribution may differ in shape or may rely on HTTPS alone.
2. If it is signed, does the existing from_google_log_list_json_verified shape generalise, or does Apple's schema differ enough to need its own parser? The schemas are known to differ.
3. If it is not signed, say so in the crate docs. A consumer pinning an unsigned list should know that the HTTPS fetch is the only thing authenticating it.

## Why it is P4

Nobody in this workspace pins Apple's list today, and the Google path is now verified. This matters when a consumer wants Apple's log-inclusion policy rather than Google's -- which is a real reason to choose it, since the two programs admit logs on different terms, and a consumer should be choosing that deliberately rather than by whichever list they found first.

## Acceptance

[ ] Apple's list distribution documented: signed or not, and how if so
[ ] If signed, either verified by the same shape or a reason recorded for why it needs its own
[ ] The crate docs say which alternative log-list sources are authenticated and which are not
